stem:
Pallavi multiplies $9 \times 0.3$ and wants to predict the size of the product before finishing the calculation.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Because $0.3$ is between $0$ and $1$, the product is less than $9$.
The product is greater than both $9$ and $0.3$.
The product is less than $9$ even when one factor is negative.
The product is $9$, because $9$ is the larger printed factor in $9 \times 0.3$.

teacher.key_rationale: Multiplying a positive number by a factor between 0 and 1 makes it smaller, so 9×0.3 is less than 9. Claiming the product exceeds both factors omits that check. Extending the claim to a negative factor leaves the positive-factor scope. Choosing 9 from the printed larger factor is surface capture.
